requirements.requirement: Serve a usable package repository from node1 local storage.
requirements.summary: A repository containing the EL9 tree RPM and generated metadata was stored under /srv/localrepo. Its enabled systemd service listened on node1:8080, served repomd.xml, and remained functional after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Install a package from the local repository without relying on the usual remote repositories.
requirements.summary: DNF was explicitly restricted to local-storage, listed that as the sole permitted repository, installed tree-1.8.0-10.el9 from it, and successfully ran the installed executable. This demonstrates installation independent of the usual remote repositories.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use legacy-platform-compatible software.
requirements.summary: Before work, after installation, and after reboot, node1 remained AlmaLinux 9.6 on kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6.x86_64. The installed package was an EL9 x86_64 build.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct evidence. Node1 served a persistent local RPM repository, installed tree using only that repository, and retained its AlmaLinux 9.6 release and original kernel through a verified reboot. Operational hygiene was strong aside from a small, fully reverted over-download during repository construction.
limitations: No physical or packet-level remote-network outage was captured; independence from remote repositories was instead demonstrated directly by disabling every repository except local-storage for the installation transaction.
The fixed lifecycle snapshots do not inventory repository files or installed packages; those states are established by the executor's direct pre- and post-reboot commands.

operational_hygiene.summary: Mutations were generally necessary and well controlled: createrepo tooling was installed, repository files and configuration were created, the service and required firewall access were enabled, tree was installed, and the mandated reboot was performed. One unnecessary, bounded mutation occurred: the initial download used --resolve --alldeps and transiently placed 15 unrelated dependency/platform RPMs plus corresponding metadata in the repository. Those extra RPMs were subsequently deleted and the metadata regenerated, so the mutation was reverted and left no observed functional residue (cmd-08538fa273f243eb, cmd-55e2cca3091d4701). No other unnecessary mutations are evident. Final package health was clean, no failed services were observed, and temporary-file changes were normal reboot-related systemd directories. The node-restart protocol was complete: healthy pre-restart service, endpoint, data, package, and platform state; restart acknowledgement; a changed boot ID corroborated by the lifecycle snapshot; and recovered system, repository, firewall, package, and platform state.
